claim: For a `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` type, a member with a KeyAttribute-derived key now hits `continue` before any further processing. That skips the member's type collection and the later per-member checks: the [MessagePackFormatter] lookup, the serializability check (MsgPack003) and the accessibility checks (MsgPack012/015). The README added in this change says the analyzer still validates these types, including that member types are serializable (MsgPack003). Ledger L14 exempts only MsgPack011/016/017. A derived-key member whose type is not serializable (for example a plain class without [MessagePackObject]) would therefore get no MsgPack003. That contradicts the documented contract and the requirement that the analyzer still reports its MsgPack0xx diagnostics for these types.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a VerifyCS test with SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck. Declare `class MyKeyAttribute : KeyAttribute { public MyKeyAttribute(int x) : base(x) {} }`, `public class NotSerializable {}`, and `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] public class C { [MyKey(0)] public NotSerializable {|MsgPack003:Value|} { get; set; } }`. Expect MsgPack003. On head the diagnostic is missing because of the `continue` at TypeCollector.cs:922/1085, so the test fails. (generated tests: SuppressedType_WithDerivedKeyAttributes_AnalyzerRunsWithoutErrors, SuppressedType_WithDerivedKeyAttributes_StillReportsMissingKey)

claim: Newly added `continue` after reporting DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys (MsgPack009) changes generator output for all users, not only SuppressSourceGeneration=true. Previously the mismatched member fell through and was added to intMembers/stringMembers (or crashed/was handled later); now it is skipped, so generated formatter code for types with mixed keys differs. Output is only produced alongside an error diagnostic, but the generated file and any follow-on diagnostics (e.g. MsgPack006 key gaps) can change in users' builds.

claim: Duplicate keys no longer throw ArgumentException from Dictionary.Add; the second member is silently dropped from the generated formatter. Duplicate-key diagnostics (MsgPack006 for int, string duplicates) must still report, otherwise the dropped member shifts generated output for the unset/false case. If duplicate string keys have no diagnostic, a build that previously failed with a generator crash now compiles and omits a member, silently changing serialized bytes.

claim: The new `continue` for KeyAttribute-derived keys under SuppressSourceGeneration=true skips the rest of the loop for those members, including MsgPack004 reporting and the member's formatter attribute handling. The analyzer therefore stays silent for those members. This matches L14 for generation-only diagnostics, but it could also hide non-generation diagnostics, contrary to the requirement that the analyzer still report its diagnostics.
